newsitem.title: CANADA: Silcorp gains on more takeover speculation.
newsitem.headline: Silcorp gains on more takeover speculation.

text.p: Convenience store operator Silcorp Ltd said shares hit a new yearly high on Monday on increased speculation that it may receive offers to fend off a hostile takeover from Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.

"I think the market believes there are other players other than Couche-Tarde," Silcorp spokesman Pat Howe said. Today Silcorp said it agreed to acquire the convenience store and diary business of the Becker Milk Co Ltd for C$12 million in cash, a C$4 million note, 950,000 Silcorp common shares and the assumption of certain liabilities.
Silcorp shares gained 0.75 to 19.05 in Toronto.
The stock passed its old high of 19.00 by as much as 0.25 but then settled back, after trading more than 170,000 shares in late afternoon.

Quebec-based Couche-Tard said today that on September 27 it had presented an sweetened offer of C$18.50 a share to Silcorp's board of directors. However, the offer expired today at 900 EDT and Couche-Tard has kept its extended bid to acquire all Silcorp shares until 900 EDT October 21.
Silcorp already rejected the original one of C$16.50 a share, made on Sept. 9.
Silcorp, which is headquartered in Toronto and already owns 520 stores, will see a 40 percent increase in its earnings per share on a yearly basis after the Becker Milk Co's acquisition, Howe said.

Couche-Tard said it considers Silcorp's proposed acquisition of certain Becker Milk's assets to be imprudent from Silcorp's perspective. Under the proposal, Becker Milk is prohibited from tendering its 950,000 Silcorp common shares to a take-over unless the bid approved by Silcorp's board.
Becker Milk's B shares closed 0.60 higher at 15.60 in very light trading in Toronto.
Couche-Tard's A shares last traded at 8.25 on September 24 on the Montreal Exchange.
